dimensions.note: firecrawlApiKey is .meta({ sensitive: true }) and vault-sourced; the key is never logged; firecrawlApiUrl hostname is matched exactly and a non-hosted target with a key logs a warning. Minor: an http:// firecrawlApiUrl is accepted, which sends the Bearer key in cleartext to a non-loopback host.

Neither fetch nor summarize logs an info-level completion line (fetch never logs succeeded/failed counts; summarize never logs that the brief was written). Per-URL refusals/failures are logged at info, not warning. The logged {url} is the raw caller-supplied URL, so any user:pass@ userinfo in it lands in logs.

Per-URL failures are soft errors carried in results; summarize validates (nonce/preamble mismatch, unparseable reply, schema) and throws before writeResource; HTTP errors include status and a body excerpt; firecrawl 401/402/429 are named. Minor: a firecrawl request timeout is reported as a generic 'request failed' rather than as a timeout.

36 tests pass, but the two load-bearing security behaviours are untested: (1) no test that a 3xx redirect to a private/metadata address is refused on the second hop (fetchOne redirect re-check has zero coverage); (2) no test of the argv runClaude passes, so nothing would catch the tool boundary being incomplete (it is: see api-contracts). No createModelTestContext test of either method's execute/writeResource path. The 'localhost resolves to loopback' test comment claims the same logic stops DNS rebinding, which it does not.
Both methods are read-only with respect to external systems and write one resource each at the end; a mid-run per-URL failure no longer aborts the batch.

BLOCKER (tool boundary): runClaude spawns `claude -p --tools ""`, but --tools only restricts the built-in tool set. MCP servers from user/project/local config and claude.ai connectors still load. Verified on this machine via the stream-json init event: with `--tools ""` the session exposed mcp__funes__get/recall/scan/sessions/sketch/status (funes connected; 'claude.ai Claude Docs' pending); adding --strict-mcp-config gave tools: [] and mcp_servers: []. So the 'summarizer holds no tools' claim is false whenever MCP is configured, and attacker-controlled page text reaches a session that can call them (subject only to the user's permission settings). Fix: add --strict-mcp-config (and consider --setting-sources "" / --bare plus a scratch cwd so hooks, plugins and the repo CLAUDE.md do not load), and assert the argv in a test. BLOCKER (egress): hostResolvesPublicly resolves with Deno.resolveDns and then fetch() resolves the hostname again independently, so the check is TOCTOU: a TTL-0 rebinding name answering public then 127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254 passes the check and connects privately. The two resolvers also differ (resolveDns ignores /etc/hosts; HTTP(S)_PROXY env makes fetch go via a proxy that resolves on its own). README ('which is also what stops a DNS-rebinding host...') and the test comment claim the opposite. Fix: pin the connection to the vetted address (or route via an enforcing egress proxy), or at minimum retract the rebinding claim and document the residual risk. Follow-up gaps: fec0::/10 and Teredo 2001::/32 not blocked; NAT64 64:ff9b:1::/48 embeddings other than /96 are unwrapped from the wrong groups; no Retry-After/backoff on firecrawl 429 (reported, not retried).

firecrawlOne adds an anonymous abort listener to ctx.signal per URL and never removes it (the leak fetchOne already fixed); runClaude likewise never removes its abort listener. firecrawlOne reads the response with res.text() unbounded and only truncates afterwards, so maxBytesPerUrl does not bound memory on that path, and truncation/bytes there count UTF-16 chars, not bytes.

README 192.168.1.1 example is intentionally accepted in quality.yaml (it demonstrates refusal of RFC1918). No other real IPs, internal hostnames, account IDs or local paths found in README.md, DESIGN.md or tests; test addresses are range-boundary values.
All schemas are plain z.object without .passthrough(); BriefSchema bounds every free-text field and strips unknown keys.
Not a CRUD lifecycle model; read-only fetch/summarize by design.
fetch writes only fetched/fetched, summarize only brief/brief; each spec has a single writer and shape.
No method reads back stored state.

Model version moved 2026.08.21.1 -> .2 -> 2026.08.22.1 (adding droppedUrls, bounding brief fields) with no upgrades entries, but no version was ever published (registry: never-published), so no released data needs migrating. Any future schema change after this publish needs an upgrades entry.
